References / Poster / 411

Anja Kaiser, Cry Baby club poster, Institut fuer Zukunft

A Leipzig club poster in orange, black, and gray: a huge blackletter “Cry Baby”, vertical stretched grotesque capitals, and grainy silver shapes like petals.

Source
AIGA Eye on Design (5 September 2019): “Acid Graphics” Are the New Psychedelia
Creator
Anja Kaiser
Made
Not stated (before September 2019). The poster gives the date “Oct 9” without a year.
Style
Acid graphics (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Loud, nocturnal, dense
Evidence
Inspected the 1200 px image Anja-Kaiser-2-Cry-Baby.jpg that Eye on Design published with the article, in a scratch folder. Not stored. The object is a digital image as the magazine published it, not a named physical copy. The caption reads “Anja Kaiser, Cry Baby”.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Eye on Design shows the poster in its 2019 article on acid graphics, with the caption “Anja Kaiser, Cry Baby”.

The poster text names Institut fuer Zukunft, An den Tierkliniken 38, 04103 Leipzig, and the performers Mykki Blanco, Yves Tumor, Perera Elsewhere, and Neele.

Observed

  • The upper half is flat red-orange and the lower half near-black. A gray vertical band at the right carries the time and address, set sideways.
  • “Cry Baby” fills the upper half in a very large black blackletter, with tight, overlapping letters.
  • Gray capitals in a wide grotesque run vertically and are cut by the edges: “MYKKI BLANCO” down the right side and other letters at the left.
  • Grainy, silver-gray shapes like petals or leaves cross both halves.
  • The line-up at the bottom is set in a heavy orange grotesque, with small notes such as “live SHAME” between the names.
  • There is no chrome type and no green.

Why it belongs

The poster shows the type side of the trend: blackletter against stretched grotesques, set huge and cut by the edges. Eye on Design includes it under acid graphics. It lacks the chrome core of this record, so it marks the edge of the style.

Borrow

Set one huge blackletter word against a vertical stretched grotesque, and let both run off the edges.

Split the ground into two flat halves and let the display type cross the split.
